item.title: '2 reasons': Trump confirms he authorised CIA 'covert operation' in Venezuela
item.description: US President Trump has authorized a covert CIA operation in Venezuela, citing the release of prisoners and mental patients into the US and the flow of drugs as primary reasons. He suggested the measures aim to increase pressure on Caracas, while Venezuelan President Maduro denounced the move as a CIA-orchestrated coup. Tensions escalate as US forces engage suspected drug-smuggling vessels.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Proud Dad of US Marine’ deported by ICE agents moments after visiting pregnant daughter at California military base
item.description: Immigration officials arrested the parents of a US Marine during a visit to Camp Pendleton. The father, Esteban Rios, was deported. The mother, Luisa Rodriguez, was detained. Both had pending green card applications. This incident highlights stricter immigration enforcement affecting military families. The Marine's sister expressed distress over her parents' absence.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘As soon as I say the word’: Trump says Israel could return to Gaza if Hamas violates ceasefire, vows all hostages will be freed
item.description: US President Donald Trump declared that Israeli forces could re-enter Gaza on his command if Hamas violates the ceasefire. He stated that Israel would swiftly address Hamas's non-compliance with hostage releases. Trump emphasized Hamas must disarm, warning of forceful action if they refuse, while also mentioning international backing for his peace plan.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Is Justin Trudeau dating Katy Perry to cope with ‘mid-life crisis’? Source says he is ‘sowing his oats again’ after divorce
item.description: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau is reportedly dating pop star Katy Perry, sparking speculation about a mid-life crisis. Photographed together on a yacht, the couple's public appearances suggest a blossoming romance. Sources close to Trudeau indicate he's enjoying newfound freedom after leaving office and his marriage, exploring life outside politics with Perry, with whom he shares common interests.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US government shutdown: Judge temporarily blocks Trump administration from firing federal workers, says 'it can't be tolerated'
item.description: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration from firing federal workers during the ongoing government shutdown, citing a lack of proper consideration and a "human cost." The decision followed a legal challenge by labor unions arguing the layoff notices were an illegal attempt to pressure Congress.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Charlie Kirk sculpture showing Jesus embracing him trolled by social media: ‘Looks like a caveman’
item.description: Ave Maria University will soon feature a new sculpture of Jesus Christ embracing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, inspired by his recent death. Canadian artist Timothy Schmalz created the piece, which is expected to join the university's permanent collection next year.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: N-words, rape jokes and ‘I love Hitler’: Leaked Republican group chat reveals thousands of vile messages – here's what they said
item.description: Leaked Telegram chats reveal shocking racist, antisemitic, and violent rhetoric from young Republican leaders across multiple states. Messages included Nazi references, racial slurs, and threats. Some accused individuals have apologized, while others faced consequences, sparking outrage within the GOP and calls for accountability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pakistan-Afghanistan conflict: 5 dead, 35 injured in Kabul; explosions before temporary ceasefire
item.description: Explosions in Kabul on Wednesday killed at least five people and wounded 35, according to an Italian NGO. This occurred just hours before Pakistan and Afghanistan agreed to a 48-hour temporary ceasefire, with Pakistan stating it carried out precision strikes in response to attacks from Afghan territory.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Italy top court blocks Nord Stream suspect extradition
item.description: Italy's top court has blocked the extradition of a Ukrainian national wanted by Germany in connection with the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions. Prosecutors believe the suspect was a key figure in the sabotage. His lawyer stated the legal basis for his detention is now gone, potentially leading to his release. A second suspect remains in custody in Poland.

'Tied me up, took selfies': Greta Thunberg breaks silence on 'torture' under Israeli detention
item.description: Greta Thunberg alleges mistreatment by Israeli authorities after her detention during the Freedom Flotilla. She claims guards subjected her to physical abuse, threats, and harassment, including being tied up and having selfies taken. Thunberg emphasizes the focus should remain on the Palestinian blockade, not her personal experience.

item.title: How to import and drive your UAE car legally in India without paying import taxes
item.description: With India’s high import duties pricing out most foreign cars, a lesser-known route lets UAE-based owners legally bring their vehicles into the country without paying steep taxes. Using the Carnet de Passage system, enthusiasts can enjoy Dubai’s more accessible high-performance and luxury models on Indian roads—experiencing rare cars without the long-term financial or regulatory burden.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bears in the house: Polar giants seen chilling in abandoned Russian Arctic station; see rare images
item.description: Remarkable drone footage reveals polar bears seeking refuge in an abandoned Russian research station on Kolyuchin Island. Photographer Vadim Makhorov captured these images, showcasing the bears' adaptability as their natural sea ice hunting grounds shrink. This unusual sight highlights the impact of climate change on Arctic wildlife and their interaction with forgotten human structures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What’s really going on in the Katy Perry-Trudeau love story? Source reveals duo ‘are definitely into each other’
item.description: Pop star Katy Perry and former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau are reportedly "definitely into each other," with sources highlighting a mutual respect and intellectual bond. Their rumoured romance, which began in July 2025, has been fueled by shared interests and a "supersized attraction," despite busy schedules. Recent viral yacht photos captured visible public displays of affection between the pair.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan declare 48-hour ceasefire: Dozens killed in border clashes - who asked for truce first?
item.description: Pakistan and Afghanistan have agreed to a 48-hour ceasefire starting Wednesday evening, following a week of deadly cross-border clashes. This truce, requested by the Afghan Taliban, aims to de-escalate tensions and facilitate dialogue. The agreement follows Pakistan's precision strikes in Kandahar and Kabul in retaliation for attacks that claimed the lives of 23 Pakistani soldiers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Boris Johnson former aide Dominic Cummings claims China ‘stole’ UK state secrets — and Whitehall buried it
item.description: Dominic Cummings alleges China compromised the UK's "Strap" data system for years, stealing top-secret intelligence. He claims senior officials covered up the breach, prioritizing relations with Beijing over national security. This revelation coincides with fallout from a collapsed Chinese espionage prosecution.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Sahil Majothi? Indian student ‘framed’ by Russia into joining war, now in Ukrainian Custody
item.description: A 22-year-old Indian student, Sahil Majothi, became the first Indian national detained in the Ukraine war after allegedly being forced to fight for Russia to avoid a prison sentence. Framed in a drug case, he was offered a choice between fighting or jail, leading to his capture by Ukrainian forces.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US passports rank drop from Henley Passport Index 2025: Top 10 strongest passports in the world revealed
item.description: The US passport has dropped to 12th place, its lowest ever, losing ground to Asian nations like Singapore and South Korea which now lead global travel freedom. This shift, driven by changing visa policies and growing Asian influence, means US citizens face more travel hurdles. European passports, meanwhile, continue to strengthen their international access.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indian-origin Subu Vedam to be deported after 43 years in US jail, family says ‘he doesn’t speak Hindi’
item.description: After 43 years wrongly imprisoned for murder, Indian-origin Subramanyam Vedam was exonerated and ordered released, only to be detained by ICE for deportation. Despite growing up in Pennsylvania and having no ties to India, a decades-old order based on his wrongful conviction now threatens to send him to a country he last saw as an infant.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
